Cooking? Check. Baking? Check. Sewing? Ehh... could use a little bit of help
I sew for money. Are you just looking to get into family repairs or do you eventually what to be making all your home decor and dressing the family?
Mostly household repairs. Hemming for shorter pants, etc. It would be great to get to a level where I could actually do that, but for now, just more everyday practical application

I really recommend the Reader's digest complete guide to sewing. It covers all the basic skills, has lots of detailed pictures and diagrams and can be frequently purchased cheaply used.

For a beginner's machine, don't spend a lot and buy a older machine. New machines are full of plastic parts that can't be repaired. Find a repair shop and ask specifically for a older machine. spend around $80-$120 and don't shy away from a 60-70 year old machine. Ask around at fabric stores to find a sewing machine repair person and pick up an old work horse and have the shop show you how to thread it and oil it. The reader digest manual has a section about learning to use sewing machines.

Don't spend a lot of money on supplies as a newbie. Buy the cheap thread and scrap fabric and get an iron and some 90/14 universal needles and a wheel of hand sewing needles.

Then you just practicing seeing bits of squares and making straight lines for a awhile and then you give advanced squares like pillowcase and curtains a try.

Sewing is a skill not a talent do you will get better with practice rather quickly.
